sealed.statement: Define and prove the critical-placement convergence evaluator: for a critical system partition, spread means the required replica count on that many DISTINCT nodes each holding a quorum-voting partition replica, not a logical replica count that three seed-local replicas already satisfy. This slice defines the invariant and its evaluator only; wiring it into the formation barrier and TRAFFIC_READY is a later slice.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

The critical partition set is read from CRITICAL_SYSTEM_PARTITION_IDS (system-partition-classification.js), the required replica count from getInitialReplicaIds (system-table-schemas-constants.js), the voter test from isVoterRaftRole (raft/replica-voter-readiness.js), and the service type from SERVICE_TYPE. The evaluator re-derives none of them locally and hardcodes no replication factor or role list.

Convergence for a critical partition is the count of DISTINCT node IDs each holding an active, quorum-voting partition replica of THAT partition, and must be >= the required replica count. Three replicas on one node is not converged; learners and non-partition services are not eligible capacity; rows for another partition never contribute.

The answer is invariant under ambient mutation of Array, Object, Set and String prototypes, including Set.prototype.forEach and Set.prototype.values: Sets are drained through a captured iterator and every row field is read through an own-property descriptor.

The evaluator is a pure projection over supplied rows: it mints no readiness verdict, no lifecycle transition and no cluster-ACTIVE or READY answer, and nothing derives ACTIVE or READY from nodes.status, publication counts, or coverage.
Absent, empty or unreadable placement evidence is NOT converged, with a typed reason; absence is never treated as satisfaction and is never skipped.

No existing readiness, barrier, routing or lifecycle behaviour changes in this Quest; nothing yet consumes the evaluator; system-table creation keeps its seed-local initial representation; ratchet baselines are not raised.

Every guard the evaluator relies on has a receipt that reds when that guard is removed: partition_id, voter role, service type, and the captured Set iterator were each verified by mutation to flip exactly one receipt red. A receipt that cannot fail is not evidence.
classification-vocabulary-unchanged lives in a test file that does NOT import the evaluator, so it stays green when the evaluator is absent and reds only on real vocabulary drift.

evidence: verifier review-996124c6028aa8d5383718dd: transposing the two count arguments at the call site left the bar 15/0 green, so no receipt showed the projection can return converged true at all; the sealed bar was consistent with an always-false evaluator

mechanism: Every rejection on this frontier has been the same shape: a receipt whose name or detail asserted more than any assertion could distinguish. Round 1 pinned .forEach and .values but not Set.prototype[Symbol.iterator], so rewriting the drain to [...values] survived green. Round 2 asserted converged === (pending === 0 && partitions > 0), a restatement of the implementation that is a tautology under the live 45-partition set. Round 3 pinned the extracted predicate but never asserted the projection can return true at all, so transposing its two count arguments — which makes convergence unobservable for every input — left the bar green. In each case the evaluator was correct; the observation layer could not tell.
intervention: Add the missing POSITIVE whole-set witness: rows spreading every declared critical partition across its required distinct voting nodes, asserting converged true, no pending partitions, and per-partition CONVERGED. Then state the empty-set receipt's scope precisely: it pins the decision helper including its empty case, while the projection's USE of that helper is established by inspection, because a call site inlining pendingCount === 0 is behaviourally identical for every reachable input.
expectedMovement: Argument transposition at the call site moves from 15 pass / 0 fail to 15 pass / 1 fail, reddening exactly the new scenario; all 16 carried receipts keep their existing single-scenario discrimination.
negativeResultMeans: If transposition still leaves the bar green, the positive witness is not exercising the whole-set projection and the scenario is itself vacuous.
discriminator: Run the mutation, not the suite: transpose the two arguments and require exactly one scenario to red. A bar that stays green under a mutation making convergence unobservable is not evidence, regardless of receipt count.

evidence: verifier review-6755563fb3fa70ee65ebc2cc: the whole-set fixture was uniform, so filtering every partition against a fixed services-p1 left the bar 16/0 green; per-partition attribution had no receipt at all

mechanism: Round 4 confirms the recurring shape at a new level: the fixture, not the assertion. The positive whole-set scenario gave all 45 critical partitions the IDENTICAL node set (node-0, node-1, node-2), so measuring the wrong partition returned the same answer as measuring the right one. Filtering every partition's rows against a fixed services-p1 left the bar 16/0 green. No other scenario caught it either: every single-partition scenario already uses services-p1, so pinning the filter there is a no-op for them, and the vocabulary scenario runs on an empty row set and compares ids without ever taking a measurement. Production effect is worse than the previous transposition: convergence for all 45 critical partitions decided by one partition's placement, so a cluster with services-p1 spread and nodes-p1 not would report whole-set convergence.
intervention: Add a scenario that omits exactly one named critical partition's rows and asserts pendingPartitionIds deep-equals that one id, which pins per-partition attribution directly; and make fixture node ids vary by partition index as well as replica index, so a row measured against the wrong partition lands on the wrong node set.
expectedMovement: Filtering every partition against a fixed services-p1 moves from 16 pass / 0 fail to 16 pass / 1 fail, reddening exactly the new scenario; all 17 carried receipts keep single-scenario discrimination.
negativeResultMeans: If the mis-attribution mutation still leaves the bar green, the omitted-partition assertion is not actually reading per-partition state and the scenario is itself uniform.
discriminator: Uniformity in a fixture is the same failure as a tautology in an assertion: if every input element is interchangeable, no assertion over them can distinguish which element was measured. Vary the fixture along the axis the code is supposed to discriminate on.

mechanism: Round 5 refines the rule rather than repeating it. The attribution scenario omitted exactly ONE partition and asserted that partition's literal id, so the fixture was uniform in CARDINALITY and the assertion shared a literal with the fixture. Two mutations passed at 17/0: capping pendingPartitionIds at one entry (an ordinary accumulation bug), and pushing the constant 'nodes-p1' instead of the measured partitionId. The second is the sharp one — the receipt added to prove attribution is measured was satisfied by an implementation that hardcodes the very value the assertion checks. converged stays correct under both; only pendingPartitionIds is wrong, but that field names WHICH partition blocks formation, so an operator would always be told nodes-p1 whatever the truth.
intervention: Omit TWO named critical partitions and assert pendingPartitionIds deep-equals both, sorted. Two makes the expected value underivable from any single constant and is the first assertion anywhere pinning that list with more than one element.
expectedMovement: cap-at-one and constant-push each move from 17 pass / 0 fail to 16 pass / 1 fail, reddening exactly this scenario; the carried mis-attribution mutation still reds exactly this scenario.
negativeResultMeans: If either mutation still passes, the assertion is still derivable from a constant and the omission count must rise again.
discriminator: An observation can only distinguish outcomes it can produce differently. A tautology makes both implementations compute the same expression; a uniform fixture makes all elements produce the same data; a single-instance fixture makes the collection produce only one shape. Vary the fixture along every axis the code must discriminate on INCLUDING cardinality, and derive the expected value independently of the input that produced it so a constant cannot satisfy it.

mechanism: Round 6 is the first hole that changes an ANSWER rather than a diagnostic. Both whole-set fixtures made every pending partition pending for the same cause — zero rows — so a present-but-under-spread partition, the exact defect the quest opened against, appeared in no whole-set fixture. Pushing pending on distinctNodeCount === 0, or on EVIDENCE_ABSENT, therefore passed at 17/0. Because converged is derived from pendingPartitionIds.length, an under-spread partition then never enters the list and the cluster is declared CONVERGED with a seed-local critical partition: the RF-only false positive this quest exists to kill. Two further survivors at 17/0: a constant PAIR (two omissions defeat a single constant, not a pair) and a list capped at TWO.
intervention: Vary three axes at once in the attribution scenario: three pending partitions instead of two; chosen BY INDEX from the sorted declared set rather than by literal name; and for MIXED causes — two omitted entirely, one given its full replica set on a single node. Assert both reason codes explicitly so the fixture cannot drift back to a single cause.
expectedMovement: distinctNodeCount-keyed, EVIDENCE_ABSENT-keyed, constant-pair and cap-at-two each move from 17 pass / 0 fail to 16 pass / 1 fail, reddening exactly this scenario.
negativeResultMeans: If any of the four still passes, the fixture is still uniform along an axis the code discriminates on and the enumeration of causes is incomplete.
discriminator: An observation can only distinguish outcomes it can produce differently, so TWO criteria apply, not one: (1) reject if an expected value is derivable from literals the fixture also supplies; and (2) reject if the fixture reaches an outcome by only one of the several causes the code can reach it by. Operationally: enumerate the reasons the code can reach an outcome and make the fixture reach it by each reason at least once.

mechanism: Round 7 widens the criterion rather than repeating it. Applying cause-enumeration only to the FAILURE outcome left the CONVERGED outcome collapsed: every converged partition in every fixture reached convergence by distinct === required, and none by distinct > required, so narrowing the bound to === passed 17/0. That narrowing is a liveness defect — on any cluster larger than the replication factor, rebalancing or learner promotion produces over-spread and formation is never observable as complete. Separately the fourth reason code REQUIRED_COUNT_UNKNOWN was asserted nowhere, so deleting its guard turned a fail-closed refusal into fail-OPEN at 17/0, violating the sealed fail-closed-typed constraint. Counting reason CODES would have called the converged side complete: it has one code but two input shapes.
intervention: Add the two missing input shapes inside existing scenarios, so no receipt id changes: a fourth replica on a fourth node asserting converged with distinct > required; and a partition whose table declares no replica IDs, with three real rows on three distinct nodes, asserting converged false with REQUIRED_COUNT_UNKNOWN.
expectedMovement: Narrowing >= to === reds the over-spread scenario; deleting the unknown-requirement guard reds the declared-count scenario; each moves from 17 pass / 0 fail to 16 pass / 1 fail.
negativeResultMeans: If either mutation still passes, the input-shape enumeration is still incomplete for that outcome.
discriminator: Enumerate the causes of EVERY outcome, not just the failure outcome, and count distinct input SHAPES rather than distinct reason codes — one code can be reached by several shapes, and a code-level enumeration declares such an outcome complete when it is not.

mechanism: Round 8: my input-shape enumeration was complete over the DECLARED domain but omitted the non-canonical container and record class entirely. No fixture anywhere contained a Proxy, an accessor-backed field, a sparse array, an Array subclass, an array-like, a symbol-keyed row or an inherited-only row, so the whole row-input hardening layer was unpinned. Replacing copyDenseOwnDataRecordArray with a bare Array.isArray check passed 17/0 while changing answers: a Proxy row among two valid ones, an Array-subclass container and a symbol-keyed row all reported converged TRUE, and a sparse array crashed. The contrast that names the gap: the Set-iteration seam had a dedicated hostile-prototype scenario while the row-input seam — the one a real caller reaches, since rows arrive from a cache rather than a literal — had none.
intervention: Extend absent-evidence-is-not-converged with all six non-canonical shapes, asserting each yields converged false with the typed evidence-absent reason AND does not throw, plus an assertion that a field accessor never executes. Record explicitly that the inner descriptor read is defence in depth and is NOT pinned, because with the strict copy running first the two reads are byte-identical for every shape and no assertion can distinguish them.
expectedMovement: Replacing the strict-own-data copy with a bare Array.isArray check moves from 17 pass / 0 fail to 16 pass / 1 fail, reddening exactly this scenario; removing both layers together also reds exactly this scenario.
negativeResultMeans: If the mutation still passes, the hostile shapes are being normalised before they reach the guard and the fixture is not exercising the seam.
discriminator: Enumerate input shapes over the CONTAINER and RECORD kinds as well as the value domain. A domain-complete enumeration that assumes canonical arrays of canonical objects leaves the entire hardening layer unobserved, and hardening is exactly the code whose absence is silent on well-formed input.

mechanism: Round 9: the container-kind enumeration was one level short. My hostile fixtures wrapped a ROW in a Proxy, refused by the record check in copyStrictOwnDataRecord, but never wrapped the CONTAINER, which is refused by a separate guard at the top of copyDenseOwnDataArray. Neutering only that container guard made a Proxy over three valid rows report distinctNodeCount 3 and converged TRUE at 17/0 green — another silent false convergence of the same class I had just closed for rows. A defence-per-level structure needs a fixture per level; enumerating hostile kinds without enumerating the levels they are checked at leaves the outer level unobserved.
intervention: Add one fixture entry — a Proxy over the row array — to the existing hostile list in absent-evidence-is-not-converged, asserting converged false with the typed evidence-absent reason and no throw. Record that the inner descriptor read, while unpinnable in isolation, IS pinned in combination because removing both layers reds the scenario.
expectedMovement: Neutering the container-level isProxy guard moves from 17 pass / 0 fail to 16 pass / 1 fail, reddening exactly this scenario.
negativeResultMeans: If it still passes, the Proxy is being unwrapped before the guard and the fixture does not reach the container level.
discriminator: Enumerate the LEVELS a defence is applied at, not just the hostile kinds: one fixture per kind per level. A kind that is checked at two levels needs a fixture at each, because a fixture at the inner level alone leaves the outer guard removable in silence.

mechanism: Round 10 closes the enumeration by auditing the fail-closed path guard by guard rather than shape by shape. Three guards were independently removable with the bar green at 17/0, two of them answer-changing: the typeof-string pin in this module's own normalizeNonEmptyString (a numeric node_id coerces to '3' and becomes a counted failure domain, converged TRUE); the null/primitive-row check in copyStrictOwnDataRecord (a null row crashes with TypeError instead of failing closed); and the descriptor enumerability clause (a present-but-non-enumerable node_id is counted, converged TRUE). The third is a distinct shape from the accessor row, which has no value field at all, so the accessor fixture never reached it.
intervention: Add one fixture per guard: a numeric node_id in malformed-node-id-rows-do-not-count, and a null row plus a non-enumerable node_id row in the hostile list. Record the guards deliberately left unpinned WITH their measured reasons: length-descriptor and safe-integer-length are unreachable, row-is-an-Array is redundant with the canonical-prototype check, and the reflectOwnKeys try/catch is dead.
expectedMovement: Each of the three removals moves from 17 pass / 0 fail to 16 pass / 1 fail, reddening exactly the scenario that owns it.

mechanism: Round 11 closes the path. Two remaining gaps, one answer-changing: INITIAL_REPLICA_IDS is a plain object literal, so an inherited key resolves — getInitialReplicaIds('constructor') returns a FUNCTION whose .length is 1. Only arrayIsArray stood between that and a replica count borrowed from Object itself: weakened to truthiness, a partition id of constructor-p1 with three distinct voters reports converged TRUE where correct code refuses, at 17/0 green. Partition ids come from data, so the input is reachable. Second, the deliberate nested freezes were unpinned: the bar asserted Object.isFrozen on the outer objects only, so removing the inner freezes left distinctNodeIds and pendingPartitionIds mutable in place at 17/0 while no computed answer changed — and pendingPartitionIds is exactly the array a formation barrier would hold.
intervention: Add an inherited-key case (constructor-p1 with three distinct voters, asserting required 0 / converged false / REQUIRED_COUNT_UNKNOWN) to the scenario that already owns the undeclared-table case, and extend the existing isFrozen assertions to the three nested arrays.
expectedMovement: Weakening the replica-list type check to truthiness reds the declared-count scenario; dropping either nested freeze reds the projection scenario; each moves 17 pass / 0 fail to 16 pass / 1 fail.
negativeResultMeans: If a mutation still passes, the fixture does not reach the guard — and a mutation harness that does not assert the patch changed the file cannot tell that case apart from a pinned guard.
discriminator: A lookup into a plain object literal resolves inherited keys, so a declared-set membership question must be answered from an OWN entry; and an immutability contract must be asserted at every level it claims, because freezing a container leaves its array values mutable. Additionally the mutation harness itself must assert the patched text differs from the original, or a green run means either pinned or never-mutated.
